idea: The fast small-model extraction collapsed retrieval because the free-text search_terms (vector query) diverges in phrasing. Hypothesis: rebalance the hybrid search toward grounded keywords (BM25) so the fast model's grounded keywords/country dominate and the divergent vector query matters less, making cheap fast extraction retrieval-equivalent to the expensive model -> speed AND preserved accuracy. Attacks the extraction->retrieval fragility root cause directly.
setup: pre-extracted baseline (gemma) and fast (gpt-oss compact+country-enum) fields for 116 distinct questions once; then searched both under 4 hybrid-weight configs, each via its own isolated OpenSearch pipeline (production 'hybrid-pipeline' untouched, verified intact and exp pipelines deleted). Metric: fast-vs-baseline retrieval fidelity.
finding: Directionally confirmed but incomplete. Increasing keyword (BM25) weight recovers fast-path fidelity from Recall 0.284 (vector-heavy) to 0.396 (keyword-heavy), then PLATEAUS (0.395 at 0.90). So the extraction->retrieval fragility decomposes into: ~a recoverable vector-phrasing component (Recall 0.28->0.40 via rebalancing) and a dominant, IRREDUCIBLE component from the fast model extracting different KEYWORDS/terms than the big model, which retrieval rebalancing cannot fix. Cheap fast extraction still cannot match the expensive model's retrieval even under keyword-grounded search.
contribution: A quantitative decomposition of why cheap model-substitution breaks retrieval: only ~part of the divergence is search-query phrasing (fixable by hybrid rebalancing); the majority is model-intrinsic keyword divergence. This rules out 'just make retrieval keyword-robust' as a fix and reinforces that the accuracy-preserving path must keep the same extraction model and accelerate it losslessly (n-gram spec).
